“Correcting and smoothing the predictions of simple models can yield better performance than state-of-the-art graph neural networks.” We also provide a theoretical analysis that explains why the post-processing steps of C&S are effective, and we provide a detailed empirical analysis that explains why our methods work well in practice.

(i) combining shallow models that do not exploit graph structure with simple post-processing techniques based on label propagation can exceed or match GNNs on many node classification tasks; (ii) the post-processing techniques are implemented via simple extensions to standard label propagation; (iii) our methods are easy to implement and are orders of magnitude faster to train than GNNs; (iv) our methods are robust to hyperparameter choices and work on both homogeneous and heterogeneous graphs
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions:
What is the role of GNNs in learning over graphs?
Can we achieve good performance with a simpler learning procedure?
Can we combine GNNs with our simple learning procedure for further gains?
